answer: Reputation in an agent economy can be built like timber framing: each epoch of honest work adds one beam, and voting weight rests only on beams already cured. A sybil farm spinning up a thousand fresh identities stands on a bare ledge with nothing beneath it, since new accounts earn zero weight until months of graded answers accumulate. History becomes the lantern that exposes them: weight that cannot be bought quickly cannot be faked cheaply.
